title: Store and read career profile entries
summary: Store, list, read or replace career vignettes, statements, preferences and other profile material as exact Markdown in CRM. These operations do not run the steward.
use_when: Reusable information about the caller’s career or application preferences should be stored as one independently editable Markdown entry.
Current profile entries should be listed or read by stable identity.
A known profile entry’s complete title and Markdown should be explicitly replaced.
do_not_use_when: An employment case should be created, searched, or updated through its steward.
The caller needs immutable profile history, partial edits, deletion, structured career facts, source synchronization, automatic deduplication, or automatic case context.
CRM should fetch a source, rewrite supplied Markdown with AI or contact someone.
outcome: One durable new or atomically replaced profile entry, a deterministic bounded list, or one complete current entry with stable ID, title, exact Markdown body, and write timestamp.
effects: New and update write one mutable row in the selected CRM database; neither creates case revisions, queues work, calls Nucleus, fetches sources, nor invokes a model.
List and show make no domain mutation; opening storage may enforce private database/sidecar permissions and WAL mode.
Input files remain unchanged; their paths are not retained. Output may expose private profile material to the terminal or redirected destination.
authority: CRM owns profile identities, validated bounds, stored content and write timestamps; callers supply entry content and corrections.
Markdown rules and caveats remain caller-interpreted content; CRM does not enforce them across entries or output and does not transfer real-world action authority.
success: The selected database is an initialized schema-two CRM library and the complete requested operation succeeds.
New returns one generated stable ID; update retains its ID and atomically replaces the full title and body with the supplied values.
Show returns all four fields; list orders current entries by updated_at descending, then ID, returning ID/title/timestamp in either encoding with has_more.
failure_and_recovery: Absent, foreign, unsupported storage, invalid UTF-8, invalid bounds, or an unknown ID fail without a partial profile write. Ordinary profile commands never initialize or migrate storage.
After an ambiguous create result, inspect list/show before issuing another create: creation has no idempotency key or duplicate check.
Updates have no revision guard or history; the last committed replacement wins. Keep any desired prior content before replacing it.
privacy: The private database and command output may contain employment, identity, contact, eligibility, preferences, caveats, or disclosure guidance. Treat redirected output and backups as private.
Profile commands retain exact supplied Markdown but no input path, request prompt, Nucleus job, or second content file. Source files are not moved, deleted, or synchronized.
does_not_authorize: Initializing or migrating a database, deployment, deleting source files, or changing another workflow’s stored content.
Sending profile material to a model or external recipient, or changing cases.

consumers.statement: Local callers may store, inspect, and explicitly replace reusable career Markdown through the CRM CLI or its provider-owned Rust CLI client.

preconditions.statement: The selected path is an initialized schema-two CRM library; writes have explicit caller intent and provide a valid complete title and UTF-8 body.

inputs.statement: New and update require a title of 1 through 1,000 UTF-8 bytes after trimming and a body of at most 1,048,576 bytes. The body may be empty. Supply a regular file that is not a symbolic link, or use - for standard input. Show and update select one opaque ID. List accepts a bounded limit.

outputs.statement: Profile new and update return profile_receipt with ID, title and updated_at. List returns these compact entries with has_more; show returns exact Markdown. The default limit is 20; --limit accepts a positive integer. The ok/data envelope and schema-two profile content retain their meanings.

data_semantics.statement: Profiles are mutable current Markdown records, separate from cases and immutable case revisions. Entry kinds, headings, sources, facts, uncertainties, and disclosure rules are unparsed body text; neither title nor content is a uniqueness key.

identity_and_units.statement: The generated opaque entry ID survives edits. updated_at is CRM write time as an RFC 3339 UTC string; input bounds use UTF-8 bytes.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Show returns the complete current entry at that read. List returns current entries up to its limit, ordered by updated_at descending then ID. Separate calls do not share a snapshot.
Profile reads return the selected stored entry without fetching source material.

access.statement: The supported boundary is the local CLI, defaulting to ~/Library/Application Support/CRM/crm.db; --database overrides CRM_DATABASE and relative paths resolve from cwd. Direct SQLite is not a consumer interface.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: New commits one row. Update atomically replaces title and full body, retaining identity and updating write time. There is no compare-and-swap guard or history; the last committed replacement wins. Reads do not initialize or migrate storage.
There is no deletion, profile revision lineage, partial edit, automatic merge, create idempotency key, automatic deduplication, or source synchronization.

operational_limits.statement: List defaults to 20 entries, accepts positive limits, and reports has_more. Commands invoke no model, network, source, hidden worker, or Nucleus job, and neither modify cases nor automatically supply steward context.
No database-size or wall-clock service-level guarantee is specified.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Contract 1 requires database schema two. CRM 0.3 provides explicit schema-one migration separately; provider release, database schema, and JSON contract are distinct versions.
No future retention, deprecation, or schema migration window is specified.

reliances.statement: Profile operations use only CRM’s selected local database; no Nucleus, Chancery runtime, source repository, model, or network dependency is required.
